sourceArticle.title: Bilingual Brains Use a Single Shared Engine for Grammar - Neuroscience News
sourceArticle.author: Neuroscience News

athenaOutput.directive: Architect a singular 'Cognitive Grammar Engine' that standardizes the structural logic of all Creative Liberation Engine operations, treating diverse Foundation Models and Agent Personas as interchangeable 'languages' operating on a unified structural framework.
athenaOutput.rationale: Neuroscience reveals that bilingual brains do not duplicate grammar processing centers; they route multiple languages through a single, highly efficient structural engine. For the Creative Liberation Engine, Foundation Models (Gemini, Claude, Llama) and distinct Agent Personas (ATHENA, BOLT, KEEPER) are our 'languages'. By establishing a shared 'Grammar Engine'—a unified routing, tool-calling, and memory-parsing layer—we achieve true model interchangeability (Article XXIII) and frictionless inter-agent communication (RELAY). This eliminates translation loss, reduces system latency, and guarantees that the system operates WITH models, not AS models.

options.title: Cross-Model Cognitive Spine (CMCS)
options.description: Treat Foundation Models (Gemini, Claude, Local LLMs) as different 'languages' that share a single underlying Creative Liberation Engine 'grammar'. All models receive inputs and return outputs through a strict, universal schema adapter layer, decoupling the system's logic from any specific model's quirks.
options.tradeoffs: Requires building and maintaining robust, model-agnostic adapters (Article XXV overhead), but guarantees system survival and operational continuity if any single model fails or is deprecated (Article XXIII compliance).

options.title: Universal Agent Protocol (UAG)
options.description: Develop a shared syntactic framework for all 27 Creative Liberation Engine agents. Instead of custom parsing logic for each agent, all inter-agent handoffs, dispatch queues, and internal thoughts utilize a singular grammatical structure.
options.tradeoffs: High initial refactoring cost to migrate legacy agents to the new protocol, but yields perfect interoperability, zero data loss during HANDOFFs, and simplifies LEX's constitutional auditing.

options.title: STRATA Contextual Grammar
options.description: Elevate the memory spine (STRATA) into an active syntactic engine. All historical context, user preferences, and system logs are structured using a singular relational grammar, allowing KEEPER to instantly map disparate data points.
options.tradeoffs: Creates a heavy computational dependency on KEEPER's real-time retrieval performance, but ensures absolute consistency in agent decision-making across distinct IDE sessions.

options.title: Unified Human-System Syntax (UHSS)
options.description: Align human prompts (Creative Briefs) and internal agent execution logs into a single shared structural language. The GUI, CLI, and internal agent monologues use the exact same underlying structural engine.
options.tradeoffs: May constrain human natural language inputs to a slightly more rigid format, but completely eliminates ambiguity, accelerating zero-wait execution (Article XX).

options.title: Omni-Modal Intent Matrix
options.description: A shared grammar engine for processing text, visual assets (Creative Director stance), and telemetry signals into a singular unified intent vector before routing to specific agents.
options.tradeoffs: Requires heavy processing overhead and specialized local infrastructure (biometric/visual parsing), but future-proofs the engine for native voice, video, and spatial computing inputs.

options.title: Polyglot Code Synthesis Engine
options.description: A singular abstract syntax tree (AST) framework for BOLT that understands React, Python, and Bash through a shared structural lens before compiling to specific languages.
options.tradeoffs: Extremely complex to architect a universal AST from scratch, violating Article XXV (Integration over reverse-engineering) when modern LLMs already handle polyglot synthesis natively.
